title: Projective Algebraic Sets Projective Morphisms and Cones

items.title: Projective space as scalar-equivalence classes
items.strategy: Fix an algebraically closed base field k and define P^n(k) as nonzero (n+1)-tuples modulo nonzero scalar multiplication, including the n=0 convention.

items.title: Homogeneous polynomials and homogeneous ideals
items.strategy: Define a homogeneous polynomial by total degree and a homogeneous ideal as one containing every homogeneous component of each of its elements.

items.title: A homogeneous zero locus is well-defined on projective points
items.strategy: Use F(lambda a)=lambda^d F(a) for degree d to show that vanishing is independent of the chosen representative.

items.title: Projective algebraic set
items.strategy: Define V_+(S) and V_+(J) using homogeneous equations, with the empty family and the irrelevant ideal conventions explicit.

items.title: Projective Zariski topology
items.strategy: Verify finite unions and arbitrary intersections of homogeneous zero loci by products and homogeneous ideal sums, then declare these closed sets.

items.title: Standard projective opens are affine spaces
items.strategy: On D_+(x_i), normalize x_i=1 and give the explicit mutually inverse coordinate maps to A^n; retain the x_0 chart for subsequent closure conventions.

items.title: Homogenization and dehomogenization
items.strategy: Define f^h in k[x_0,...,x_n] and F(1,x_1,...,x_n), prove the degree bookkeeping, and state the correspondence after removing powers of x_0.

items.title: Projective closure of an affine algebraic set
items.strategy: Embed A^n as D_+(x_0) in P^n and define the projective closure as the Zariski closure of that image.

items.title: Saturation of a homogeneous ideal
items.strategy: Define J:x_0^infinity as the set of G for which x_0^r G lies in J for some r, and record its homogeneous-ideal property.

items.title: Ideal of a projective closure via saturation
items.strategy: For A=V(I) with I=I(A), compare the D_+(x_0) chart with the affine zero set of I and use affine Nullstellensatz to prove I_+(closure A)=(I^h:x_0^infinity), avoiding the false unsaturated-generator formula.

items.title: Homogeneous coordinate ring
items.strategy: Define S(X)=k[x_0,...,x_n]/I_+(X) as a graded homogeneous coordinate ring, distinguishing it from a global-function ring.

items.title: Classical projective variety
items.strategy: Define a classical projective variety to be an irreducible projective algebraic set over the fixed algebraically closed field.

items.title: Irreducibility and homogeneous prime ideals
items.strategy: Pass between the affine cone and its projective quotient to prove the projective Nullstellensatz consequences: irreducibility corresponds to a proper homogeneous prime vanishing ideal.

items.title: Regular functions on a projective variety
items.strategy: Define regularity locally through degree-zero homogeneous fractions G/H on standard opens, with H homogeneous and nonvanishing at the point.

items.title: Compatibility of projective regular-function charts
items.strategy: Dehomogenize degree-zero fractions on overlapping standard charts and prove they agree exactly when their cross-products agree in the homogeneous coordinate ring.

items.title: Global regular functions on an irreducible projective variety
items.strategy: Use affine standard charts to clear coordinate powers, then act by the degree-zero fraction on a nonzero finite-dimensional graded piece and apply Cayley--Hamilton.

items.title: Projective morphisms in homogeneous coordinates
items.strategy: Define a morphism X to P^m locally by same-degree homogeneous coordinate functions with no common zero, rather than by an arbitrary coordinate tuple.

items.title: Homogeneous coordinate formulas define morphisms
items.strategy: Check scalar invariance and, on each target standard open, identify the coordinate ratios as regular functions that glue.

items.title: Closed projective embedding from a radical homogeneous ideal
items.strategy: For a homogeneous radical ideal J with nonempty V_+(J), use the projective Nullstellensatz consequence to identify I_+(V_+(J))=J; the inclusion V_+(J) into P^n is the closed embedding and its homogeneous coordinate ring is k[x_0,...,x_n]/J.

items.title: Affine cone over a projective algebraic set
items.strategy: Define C(X) in A^{n+1} by the homogeneous ideal I_+(X), include the vertex, and state its scalar-stability convention.

items.title: The cone over a projective variety is irreducible
items.strategy: Use primeness of I_+(X) to identify the cone coordinate ring as a domain and hence the cone as irreducible.

items.title: The affine chart is dense in a projective closure
items.strategy: Unpack closure in P^n and the chosen A^n=D_+(x_0) embedding to prove that the original affine set is dense in its projective closure.

items.title: Degree of a reduced projective hypersurface
items.strategy: For a reduced hypersurface presented by a nonconstant homogeneous square-free F, define its degree as deg F and state this restricted convention explicitly.

items.title: Affine pieces of a projective hypersurface
items.strategy: Dehomogenize F on each D_+(x_i) to identify the chart with an affine hypersurface and track the degree convention.

items.title: A homogeneous coordinate ring is not the global function ring
items.strategy: Contrast the graded coordinate ring with constant global regular functions on an irreducible projective variety, including P^n as the basic warning.

title: Projective Algebraic Sets Projective Morphisms and Cones — Examples

items.title: The two standard affine charts of the projective line
items.strategy: Write U_0 and U_1 for P^1, compute their affine coordinates t and s, and verify the overlap transition s=1/t.

items.title: Projective closure of a parabola
items.strategy: Homogenize y-x^2 to yz-x^2, identify the point at infinity, and check that the x_0 chart recovers the affine parabola.

items.title: Raw homogenized generators can add a projective component
items.strategy: For I=(x-1,xy), compare V_+(x-z,xy) with its x_0-saturation, exhibit the spurious point at infinity, and show why saturation is necessary.

items.title: Standard affine charts of a projective conic
items.strategy: For XZ-Y^2=0 in P^2, dehomogenize on the standard charts and compare the resulting affine conic equations.

items.title: Affine cone over a smooth projective conic
items.strategy: Over characteristic not 2, compute C(X)=V(XZ-Y^2), show all partial derivatives vanish at the vertex, and keep this elementary hypersurface-derivative diagnostic separate from the later regular-locus theorem.

items.title: An inhomogeneous equation does not define a projective zero locus
items.strategy: Compare representatives of [1:0] under x_0+1 to show that an inhomogeneous equation has representative-dependent vanishing.

items.title: The power map on the projective line
items.strategy: For [X:Y] mapped to [X^d:Y^d], verify the no-common-zero condition and compute the two affine-chart formulas.
